definitions.gloss: deposition; accumulation; piling up in layers
definitions.explanation: The piling up of material such as sediment, snow, or debris in layers over time. In geology, the deposition of sediment that forms strata. Usually intransitive: things {堆積|たいせき}する.

examples.japanese: {土砂|どしゃ}が{堆積|たいせき}する。
{川底|かわぞこ}に{泥|どろ}が{堆積|たいせき}している。
examples.english: Mud has accumulated on the riverbed.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{年月|ねんげつ}をかけて{土砂|どしゃ}が{堆積|たいせき}し、{地層|ちそう}ができた。
examples.english: Over long years, sediment was deposited and formed strata.

notes:
Composed of {堆|たい} (heap up) + {積|せき} (accumulate).

TRANSITIVITY:
Usually intransitive — material {堆積|たいせき}する on its own. Use {堆積|たいせき}させる when an agent causes the buildup.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土砂|どしゃ}の{堆積|たいせき}: deposition of earth and sand
- {堆積物|たいせきぶつ}: sediment, deposits
- {堆積岩|たいせきがん}: sedimentary rock

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {侵食|しんしょく}: erosion — the opposite process, wearing material away
- {蓄積|ちくせき}: accumulation — used of abstract things (knowledge, fatigue) as well as physical
